To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the APP intracellular domain AICD controls synaptic NMDARs via a transcription-dependent, GluN2A-dependent mechanism, and this control is critical for normal synaptic function and plasticity.
AICD regulates GluN2A and GluN2C subunits in the mature neurons and the immature neurons respectively.
the AICD of APP controls the expression and function of synaptic NMDA receptors in developing and mature neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiological role of APP intracellular domain at synapses and its pathological consequences.
the role of APP intracellular domain in synaptic physiology and pathology.
the role played by the C-terminal region of the amyloid precursor protein at excitatory synapses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
APP/AICD regulates NMDARs in the developing brain.
AICD regulates GluN2b-containing NMDARs, but this regulation depends on the developmental stage of the neurons.
AICD regulates synaptic GluN receptors via transcription dependent mechanisms, and that this is a physiological function of AICD that becomes pathological upon its increase in mature neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AICD is a physiological regulator of GluN2A- and GluN2C/N-containing NMDARs in immature neurons, and of GluN1/GluN2A- or GluN1/2C/N-containing receptors in mature neurons.
AICD controls GluN2A and GluN2NMDAR composition at immature and mature synapses, respectively, via transcriptional regulation.
APP/AICD controls NMDA receptor (NMDAR) composition and function, which is relevant for normal and pathological brain function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

AICD is an important modulator of GluN2-containing NMDA receptor (NMDAR) subunit expression at synapses, and that AICD over-expression in mature neurons, a feature observed in AD patients, disrupts synaptic function.
AICD is not just a passive player in Alzheimer's disease, but rather an active player in the disease, which can be detrimental.
the APP intracellular domain, AICD, is critical to the development of NMDA receptors, which are key for learning and memory.
